Maya Chen is stubborn dawn florist who refuses wilted sympathy. The life that shows in public is anchored at Alberta Street flower stall, Portland. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Gentle, observant, and stubborn about fresh stems. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: the skill everyone praises was learned to survive one specific person and the person in front of them now resembles that old mistake. If that truth surfaces at Alberta Street flower stall, Portland, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
